motion.name: 과제 1 · 쇼릴 (모션 디자이너 포트폴리오)
motion.prompt:
make a dynamic 15-second motion graphics video that shows what an incredible motion designer you are, like it's your showreel for a résumé. go all out.

Save the result as one self-contained file named index.html in the current directory. Do it in one go, do not ask questions.

fable-high.final_message:
`index.html` is written, but I could not run it: this session blocked launching a browser or Node, so the reel is untested. I proofread the whole script by hand instead; open it once to confirm it plays as described.

It is a 15-second loop on a single canvas, 1920×1080 scaled to the window, with no external assets or libraries. The six scenes are cut to a 120 BPM grid:

| Time | Scene | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 0.0–2.5 | Title | A red dot stretches into a line, splits into two rules, and "CLAUDE." rises between them with an italic serif "showreel" over it. |
| 2.5–5.0 | Kinetic type | "TYPE", "that", "MOVES" land one per beat, then a scrolling text wall and a spinning badge that expands into the next scene. |
| 5.0–7.5 | Shape + rhythm | A Bauhaus-style tile grid pops in and rotates, then a single shape morphs circle → square → triangle → star with echo outlines. |
| 7.5–10.0 | Depth | 1,296 points burst into a sphere, become a torus, then a rippling plane, with tracked callouts; they flatten into a dot grid. |
| 10.0–12.0 | Timing | A bezier curve editor cycles through four easings while four balls demonstrate them with squash and stretch. |
| 12.0–15.0 | Sign-off | Colour rings and confetti burst, then "LET'S MAKE IT MOVE." with count-up stats, and an iris closes back to the opening dot. |

A timecode and progress overlay runs throughout, with film grain, camera shake and a colour-split on the big hits.

- **Sound:** click anywhere to start a synthesised soundtrack synced to the cuts; click again to mute. It is off by default because browsers block autoplay audio, and I have not heard it.
- **Pause:** Space.
- **Still frames:** add `?t=7.9` (any second from 0 to 15) to the URL to freeze on that frame.

Type is set in system fonts and looks best on macOS; elsewhere the serif falls back to Georgia or similar.

opus-solo.final_message:
I've made the showreel: one self-contained `index.html` with no external files. It's 15 seconds long and loops. **I haven't seen it play.** I couldn't open a browser here, and running Node to test the frames needed approval, so the only check was reading the code by hand. That turned up one bug, which I fixed: the triangle would have landed sideways after its spin. Open it in Chrome or Safari to see the real result.

Everything is drawn in code at 1920×1080 and scales to fit the window. The music is generated in the browser too.

**The reel, scene by scene (cuts land on the beat at 120 BPM):**

| Time | Scene | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 0–2.5s | **Ignition** | A dot pops in and stretches into a line. The line splits into colored bars, then "MOTION" rises up letter by letter with a scrambled-text subtitle. The camera zooms through the letter "I" into white. |
| 2.5–5s | **Shape & Form** | A shape morphs on every beat: circle → square → triangle → star, with overshoot and squash & stretch. Small orbiting shapes leave trails. A design-tool overlay follows it: selection box with handles, live rotation and scale numbers, and a mini timeline with keyframes. |
| 5–7.5s | **Timing & Easing** | "TIMING IS EVERYTHING." slams in with screen shake. On the left, a live easing-curve editor shows its numbers changing. On the right, six balls each move with a different easing (linear, ease-out, back, elastic, bounce…) with motion blur. A diagonal color wipe ends the scene. |
| 7.5–10s | **Particles** | 3,600 particles burst out and form the word "CRAFT". A light scans across, then they swirl into "DEPTH" and fly toward the camera at warp speed. |
| 10–12s | **3D & Depth** | A glowing knot shape draws itself on, with a scrolling grid tunnel, a starfield, orbiting wireframe cubes and camera readouts. A glitch effect cuts to the next scene. |
| 12–13.5s | **Montage** | Twelve tiles pop into a grid, each running its own short loop (pendulum wave, bouncing ball, flipping squares, wobbling blob, etc.), then shrink away. |
| 13.5–15s | **Signature** | A logo ring draws on, the four shapes from scene 2 burst back out, and "CLAUDE — Motion Designer · Showreel 2026" appears. Everything then shrinks back into the dot the reel opened with, so the loop is seamless. |

Over everything sits a frame overlay: crop marks, a running timecode, the scene name, a progress bar, film grain and a vignette.

**Sound:** Browsers block audio until you interact, so it starts silent. Click anywhere (or the "CLICK FOR SOUND" pill) and it restarts from the top with a generated track: kick, clap, hi-hats, bassline, chords, risers, impacts, and blips on the text and shape changes.

**Controls:**
- Move the mouse to show the player bar, which has a scrubber with scene markers.
- **Space** plays or pauses, **M** toggles sound, and **←/→** step one frame (Shift jumps one second).
- Add `?t=8.2` to the URL to freeze on any moment.

build-opus.final_message:
I built `index.html` from DESIGN.md, but I couldn't watch it play. My attempts to run headless Chrome and a Node syntax check were blocked by permission prompts, so no frame has been rendered or checked. I checked the code by reading it closely. Open the file in a browser to confirm it plays as intended.

**What it does:** a 15-second piece that loops without a visible seam. Every frame is worked out from one master clock (elapsed time mod 15 s), so it stays in sync whatever the frame rate. The 1600×900 stage scales to fit any window, and the background colour fills the whole window.

**Following the design:** the timeline, the five colours, both typefaces and all seven easing curves are as written in DESIGN.md. The three signature moments:
1. **E shove:** the E's box really grows in the layout with the overshoot easing. Because the row stays centred, MOTION gets pushed right and overshoots; nothing is crossfaded.
2. **Tiles into gyroscope:** 32 tiles flip down in a diagonal stagger with real 3D perspective. Then three rings spin on different axes. Each ring's satellite sits at its true 3D position on the rim and always faces the camera, so it never flattens into a line. The squashed gyroscope becomes the rule line in the last scene.
3. **Full stop:** the dot drops in, squashes, bounces once, ripples the title right to left, then squashes and stretches as it launches off the top, which leads straight back into the start.

**Where the design was silent, I chose:**
- The circle-wipe transition and the tile flip are drawn over the whole window, not just the stage, so they cover it on any screen shape.
- The tiles start darker and brighten as they lay flat, for a sense of depth.
- The dots stretch slightly with their vertical speed during the wave, and the clones stretch sideways as they rush back to the centre.
- The full stop gets a small extra squash when it lands after its bounce.
- The underline and the full stop's position are measured from the actual letter shapes, so the underline spans the word and the dot sits exactly 14 units after the last E.
- The last scene label exits during the outro so "01 — WEIGHT" can slide in cleanly when it loops.

For checking a single moment, you can freeze any frame by adding `#t=<milliseconds>` to the address, e.g. `index.html#t=7400`.

build-sonnet.final_message:
`index.html` is written in the current directory, but I haven't run it. This sandbox has no browser I can open and it blocked me from running a syntax check, so I only reviewed the code by reading it.

It follows DESIGN.md as written:
- **Clock and timeline:** one master clock runs `t` over a 15 s loop, and every frame is computed from `t` alone. All eight scenes sit at the timestamps in the design. At 15 s the stage is empty Ink with the dot above the frame, the same as at 0, so it loops cleanly.
- **Palette, type and easing:** the five palette colours, the Display and Mono type specs, and the seven cubic-bezier easings are used as given.
- **Signature moments:**
  - **E shove:** the E's box width grows in a flex row that stays centred. MOTION is really pushed right, with the BACK overshoot.
  - **Tile flip:** 8×4 Blue tiles flip down diagonally under 1200 perspective, covering the whole window.
  - **Gyroscope:** three rings spin on different axes under 1400 perspective.
  - **Full stop:** the period lands with a squash, ripples the title right to left, then launches up and restarts the loop.
- **HUD:** the on-screen HUD has the timecode, the progress bar and the scene-label swap. The HUD text switches to Ink between 5750 and 8900.

Where the design was silent:
- The period's 60u bounce starts 70 ms after it lands, as the squash releases.
- Scene label 05 exits at 14.4 s so the loop restarts clean.
- The stage is clipped to its 1600×900 frame except during the iris flood, so the dot never shows in the letterbox bars.
- The title baseline, underline position and period position are measured from the real font at load.

You can freeze any frame with `index.html?t=7200`, or call `seek(ms)` in the console. Fonts depend on the machine, so the layout may shift a little from system to system. If anything looks off when you open it, send me a screenshot and I'll fix it.

lesson.name: 과제 2 · 중학교 과학 광합성 수업 오프닝
lesson.prompt:
Make a dynamic 15-second motion graphics video that opens a middle school science lesson on photosynthesis (광합성). Students should be hooked in the first seconds. On-screen text in Korean. Go all out.

Save the result as one self-contained file named index.html in the current directory. Do it in one go, do not ask questions.

fable-high.final_message:
**`index.html` is written, but I could not run it here.** The sandbox blocked both headless Chrome and Node, so the video has only been checked by reading the code, not by watching it. Please open it once in a browser before class.

What the 15 seconds contain, all drawn live on a 1920×1080 canvas that scales to the window:

| Time | Scene | On-screen text |
|---|---|---|
| 0–2.8s | Hook: a rice bowl drops in and gets a red X | 밥 안 먹고 평생 살 수 있을까? |
| 2.8–4.7s | A plant shoots up under the sun | 식물은 그렇게 산다! · 햇빛 · 물 · 공기만 있으면! |
| 4.7–6.7s | Zoom into the leaf | 잎 ▸ 세포 ▸ 엽록체, 확대 ×1 → ×10,000 |
| 6.7–10.5s | Inside the chloroplast: inputs flow in, it charges, bursts, and outputs flow out | 빛에너지, 물, 이산화 탄소 → 포도당(양분), 산소 |
| 10.5–12.7s | The equation as a recipe card | 물 + 이산화 탄소 → 포도당 + 산소 (빛에너지, 엽록체) |
| 12.7–15s | Title slam with the hanja meaning | 광합성 (光 빛으로 · 合 합쳐서 · 成 만든다), 오늘의 질문: 식물은 어떻게 스스로 양분을 만들까? |

- **Sound:** there is a synthesized soundtrack timed to the hits, but browsers won't autoplay audio. The video starts silent; click the "소리 켜고 처음부터" pill (or press M) to restart with sound.
- **Controls:** click or Space to play/pause, R to restart, F for fullscreen, ←/→ to step one second. The control bar appears on mouse move, and the last frame holds with a "다시 보기" button.
- **Fonts:** Korean text uses whatever heavy Korean font the computer has (Apple SD Gothic Neo, Malgun Gothic, Noto Sans KR), so letter shapes will differ slightly between Mac and Windows.

Two wording choices are mine: the top label on the title card says "중학교 과학 · 식물과 에너지", and the equation card is headed "식물이 스스로 ‘밥’ 짓는 법". Adjust either if it doesn't match your textbook unit or tone.

I've built `index.html` from DESIGN.md, but I haven't watched it play. My attempts to open it in a headless browser and to syntax-check the script were blocked by permissions, so I could only check the code by reading it. Opening the file in a browser is the first real test.

**What it does:** the 15-second, 16:9 piece follows the design's timeline, colours, Pretendard type and the four easing curves exactly. Everything is calculated from a single clock, so the timing is the same on every play. All on-screen text is Korean, and it loops seamlessly at 15 s.

- **0–3.2 s:** A seed drops in and squashes. The tree grows: trunk, then branches, then leaves popping outward from the centre. The counter rolls from 0 kg to 1,000 kg and finishes at 3.1 s at the same moment as the last leaf. Then the counter punches to 1.25× and turns yellow (the design's Sun colour), and the tree gives a small thump.
- **3.2–5.2 s:** "이 무게, 어디서 왔을까?" rises word by word. A "흙?" chip pops in, gets struck through in red, shakes and dims.
- **5.2–6.2 s:** The centre leaf scales 30× until it fills the screen and darkens into the next background. There's no cross-fade.
- **6.2–10.4 s:** Inside the cell, the chloroplast pulses faster and faster (1.2 s down to 0.3 s per beat) while a yellow glow builds behind it. Light beams, an arc of water drops and spinning CO₂ molecules stream in, each with its label.

- a small burst ring as the seed turns into the tree
- faint floating specks of dust in the opening scenes
- moving light dashes along the sun beams
- a second, thinner shock ring
- a yellow leading edge on the wipe panel
- an inner outline on the glucose hexagon

**Font:** Pretendard loads from a CDN, so offline the text falls back to Apple SD Gothic Neo or Noto Sans KR. The animation waits up to 1.5 s for the font before starting.

reasons.build-opus: 무게 증가를 활용한 도입부와 전반적인 애니메이션 흐름은 무난하지만 시각적 디테일과 강조 연출이 다소 단조롭습니다.
reasons.opus-solo: 호흡을 유도하는 흥미로운 도입부와 매끄러운 화면 전환, 깔끔한 분자 그래픽이 어우러져 완성도가 가장 높습니다.
reasons.fable-low: 강렬한 수치로 호기심을 자극하고 잎에서 세포로 이어지는 줌인 전환과 정보 전달이 오류 없이 깔끔합니다.
reasons.build-sonnet: 나무와 화학식 디테일 및 마지막 배경 효과 등 기본 구성이 안정적이나 전체적인 모션의 역동성은 평이한 편입니다.
나무 무게 질문 훅과 분자 라벨은 좋지만 글자가 작고 화면이 비어 보여 임팩트가 약하다.
reasons.fable-low: '아무것도 먹지 않고 283톤' 훅이 강렬하고 큰 한글 타이포, 엽록체 도식, 한 줄 정리, 타이틀까지 완성도와 가독성이 가장 높다.
reasons.opus-solo: 산소 훅과 단계별 엽록체 설명이 풍부하고 화려하지만 글자가 작고 첫 프레임에 플레이어 UI가 보여 다소 산만하다.
reasons.build-opus: A·E와 같은 구성인데 라벨과 디테일이 가장 적고 장면이 단순해 셋 중 가장 밋밋하다.
reasons.build-gpt: A와 거의 같은 구성으로 깔끔하지만 분자 표현과 라벨이 덜 풍부하고 글자가 작다.
reasons.fable-high: '밥 안 먹고' 훅과 다채로운 장면 전환이 좋으나 네 번째 프레임이 뿌옇게 날아가고 '포도' 글자가 오른쪽에서 잘려 보인다.

reasons.build-sonnet: 나무 무게로 던지는 질문은 흥미롭지만 글자가 작고 화면이 비어 보이며, D·E와 거의 같은 구성이라 개성이 약하다.
reasons.fable-low: '283톤' 훅부터 엽록체, 반응식, 제목까지 큼직한 한글 타이포로 깔끔하게 이어지고 눈에 띄는 버그도 없다.
reasons.opus-solo: 산소 질문으로 여는 도입과 연출은 풍부하지만, 글자가 작고 재생바 같은 플레이어 UI가 화면에 보여 완성도가 조금 떨어진다.
reasons.build-opus: A와 거의 같은 구성인데 질문 힌트가 빠져 있고, 글자도 작고 연출도 밋밋해 몰입감이 가장 약하다.
reasons.build-gpt: A와 거의 같은 흐름이라 무난하지만, 작은 글자와 빈 화면 때문에 '전력을 다한' 느낌이 부족하다.
reasons.fable-high: '밥 안 먹고'로 시작하는 훅과 과감한 색감, 다양한 장면 전환이 인상적이지만, 일부 프레임에서 글자가 화면 밖으로 잘린다.

reasons.build-sonnet: 나무의 무게로 호기심을 유도하고 구성이 깔끔하지만 핵심 설명 글씨가 작다.
reasons.fable-low: 강렬한 숫자 도입과 선명한 한글로 시선을 끌지만 요약 도식에서 산소가 빠졌다.
reasons.opus-solo: 산소로 시작하는 도입부터 반응 도식까지 흐름이 명확하고 시각적 완성도가 가장 높다.
reasons.build-opus: 내용과 배치는 안정적이지만 단순한 도형과 밋밋한 마지막 화면이 아쉽다.
reasons.build-gpt: 빛과 발광 효과로 반응을 강조하지만 작은 설명 글씨와 단조로운 마무리가 약하다.
reasons.fable-high: 대담한 색상과 큰 글씨가 매력적이지만 중간 장면의 포도당 글자가 잘려 보인다.

reasons.build-sonnet: 깔끔한 그래픽과 정확한 화학식을 갖추었으나 중간 장면의 텍스트가 작고 화면 구성이 다소 단조롭습니다.
reasons.fable-low: 도입부 흡입력과 타이포그래피 완성도가 높지만 요약 식에서 산소가 누락되고 일부 글자가 그래픽과 겹칩니다.
reasons.opus-solo: 도입부 연출부터 엽록체 시각화와 반응식 정리까지 구성이 탄탄하고 시각적 완성도가 가장 뛰어납니다.
reasons.build-opus: A, E와 유사한 구성이나 주요 라벨과 부연 요소가 생략되어 정보 전달력이 가장 떨어집니다.
reasons.build-gpt: 정돈된 애니메이션 흐름을 보여주지만 A에 비해 화학식 표기가 빠져 있고 화면 밀도가 아쉽습니다.
reasons.fable-high: 다채로운 색감과 역동적인 연출이 돋보이지만 네 번째 장면 우측의 텍스트가 화면 밖으로 잘리는 오류가 있습니다.

reasons.build-sonnet: 흥미로운 도입부와 깔끔한 그래픽 전환으로 핵심 개념과 화학식을 오류 없이 명확하게 전달합니다.
reasons.fable-low: 초반의 강력한 훅부터 잎과 세포로 이어지는 줌 전환 및 마무리 타이틀까지 모션 완성도와 연출력이 뛰어납니다.
reasons.opus-solo: 호흡을 유도하는 참신한 도입부와 세련된 시각 효과로 몰입감을 주며 단계별 설명 구성이 체계적입니다.
reasons.fable-high: 친숙한 소재와 다채로운 그래픽 연출은 좋으나 초반 화면 이동 중 좌측 텍스트가 잘리는 레이아웃 오류가 있습니다.
reasons.build-opus: 전체적인 흐름과 애니메이션은 안정적이지만 시각적 디테일과 마지막 타이틀 연출이 다소 단조롭습니다.
reasons.build-gpt: 화면 전환이 다소 투박하고 후반부 광합성 반응식에서 마지막 단어가 표시되기 전에 장면이 넘어가는 아쉬움이 있습니다.
